british_columbia.text: A 2026 Ministry of Health review is examining internal patient-safety reviews and patient-initiated quality reviews, explicitly including Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination; engagement is intended to inform policy direction and possible legislative change.

Island Health paused its acute-care Indigenous self-identification program effective July 8, 2026 after First Nations feedback, separating the pause from a later redesign commitment centred on shared governance and Indigenous data sovereignty.

sources.title: Temporary Pause of the Indigenous Patient Self-Identification Program in Acute Care

british_columbia.text: B.C.'s 2026–28 Anti-Racism Action Plan commits to a Ministry of Health centre for anti-racism and cultural safety and says the first progress report is due in September 2027; this is an announced commitment, not implementation evidence.

saskatchewan.text: The First Nations Health Ombudsperson Office published its inaugural July 2023–March 2025 report, creating a strong Indigenous-led accountability source family separate from the Saskatoon cohort.

The Saskatchewan legislature records the Health Minister saying both the Ministry and Saskatchewan Health Authority were reviewing the ombudsperson report and recommendations; no later formal response was located in this bounded pass.

Federal 2025–26 UN Declaration reporting confirms that the ISC Saskatchewan Region established an Anti-Indigenous Racism Navigator Network for First Nations-organization health navigators, but gives no named participant list or outcome report.

sources.title: UN Declaration Act Action Plan 2026 reporting — Shared Priority 8

alberta.text: Current Alberta reporting groups the Indigenous Health Division, navigator and innovation funding, advisory council, and patient-safety advocate as continuing response mechanisms, while preserving their different governance and operational roles.
The broader MAPS two-year-plan page reports 13 of 30 actions completed and 17 in progress; those aggregate numbers should not be read as a status ledger for the Indigenous panel's 22 recommendations.

sources.title: Modernizing primary health care — progress on 2-year plan

alberta.text: Alberta says 11 in-person and 27 virtual sessions informed a planned What We Heard report and Indigenous Anti-Racism Strategy. The engagement page still presents the outcome as drafting work, so the final strategy remains a bounded follow-up question.

sources.title: Addressing racism in Indigenous health care

new_case_candidates.title: First Nations Health Ombudsperson inaugural reporting and response chain
new_case_candidates.evidence_depth: Indigenous-led annual report; legislated-government acknowledgement and review response; federal continuation funding context
new_case_candidates.reason: The source chain is strong enough for a separate accountability dossier, but it should not be folded into the Saskatoon coerced-sterilization cohort without case-specific evidence.

stopping_reason: High-value official updates were captured. Additional searches repeated existing sources, lacked recommendation-level disaggregation, or did not meet the significance threshold.
